methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series C → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.7x) to $1.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Waabi, a Series C transportation technology company founded by Raquel Urtasun, is evaluated against a broader transportation sector peer set of seven private companies, including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Slate Auto, and ZeroAvia. No public comparables exist in the immediate peer category.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation lens. Using the company's $1.0B total raised as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement, this method yields $1.7B. Peer-median comparison is not viable; while three same-sector peers exist, none satisfy filtering criteria for stage-alignment, adjacent-stage proximity, or valuation-tier similarity at sufficient density (minimum three required). A broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable comparability noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B to $2.0B, with a median point estimate of $1.7B. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result, acknowledging the single-method foundation. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-universe peer validation and reliance on total raised as a proxy for last-round valuation, which may not reflect current market conditions or dilution dynamics. Confidence in this range is moderate and contingent on stage-progression assumptions holding for the specific transportation subsector.
